metadata.title: Migrate workspace configuration and deployment assets
metadata.body:
Move the shared TypeScript configuration from `packages/tsconfig` to `tooling/tsconfig` and resolve it through the existing `@daphne-test/tsconfig` package identity. Update workspace registration, the lockfile, leaf configs, and root build inheritance while preserving effective compiler settings and compiled output.

Add an offline deployment-module bundle: an executable shell command performs a clean build and atomically replaces `releases/commerce.tar.gz` only after packaging succeeds. The archive contains compiled modules, explicit CommonJS package metadata for ESM consumers, and deployment documentation with a relative documentation symlink. Add a GitHub Actions workflow that installs, validates, and uploads the artifact. The API and worker remain reusable modules; no server or environment is deployed.

Validation:
- Clean `npm ci` and `npm test`: eight configuration checks and two packaging integration checks pass.
- All seven effective configurations and all 80 emitted JS/declaration file hashes match `main`; no production TypeScript files change.
- Packaging covers stale output removal, extraction inside an ESM consumer without runtime dependencies, paths with spaces, another working directory, preserved documentation symlinks, and retaining the previous archive after build/archive failures.
- Shell syntax, workflow YAML parsing, executable/symlink Git modes, and `git diff --check` verified.
- [GitHub Actions build and artifact upload passed](https://github.com/daphne-proj/pr-review-test/actions/runs/38890426498) for head `410da83eaee97864746415247d1bfbf0f559381c`.

Based directly on `main`, independently of PRs #1–#3. Daphne analysis, `ask-pr`, and evals are deferred. The packaging script targets macOS/Linux and runs one build per checkout at a time.

Fresh whole-branch review identified the ESM-consumer package boundary; a failing regression test reproduced it and passed after adding the CommonJS metadata. No other findings remain. Existing business logic and standalone leaf-build limitations are unchanged. Archive metadata is not normalized for byte-for-byte reproducibility, and packaging makes no crash-durability guarantee. Host provisioning, deployment credentials, and npm publication remain outside this module-bundling workflow.

source.text:
name: Build deployment modules

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:

permissions:
  contents: read

jobs:
  package:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v7
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: npm
      - run: npm ci
      - run: npm test
      - uses: actions/upload-artifact@v7
        with:
          name: commerce-deployment
          path: releases/commerce.tar.gz
          if-no-files-found: error
          retention-days: 7

Shared TypeScript defaults live in the `tooling/tsconfig` workspace. Apps,
packages, and the root build inherit `@daphne-test/tsconfig/base.json`; run
`npm ci` after switching to this layout to refresh workspace links.

The deployment bundle contains compiled modules, package metadata, and documentation. See the
[deployment instructions](docs/deployment.md) for prerequisites, extraction,
artifact checks, and CI behavior. No production TypeScript or runtime behavior
changes as part of this configuration migration.

#!/bin/sh
set -eu

repo_root=$(CDPATH= cd -- "$(dirname -- "$0")/.." && pwd)
cd "$repo_root"
npm run build
printf '%s\n' '{"type":"commonjs"}' > dist/package.json

mkdir -p releases
archive=$(mktemp "$repo_root/releases/.commerce.XXXXXX")
trap 'rm -f "$archive"' 0
tar -czf "$archive" dist docs/deployment.md deploy/README.md
mv "$archive" releases/commerce.tar.gz
printf '%s\n' "$repo_root/releases/commerce.tar.gz"

# Deployment module bundle

Use Node 22, npm, a POSIX shell, and tar/gzip on macOS or Linux. From the
repository root:

```sh
npm ci
npm test
npm run package:deployment
```

The shared TypeScript configuration now lives in `tooling/tsconfig`. All apps,
packages, and the root build resolve it as `@daphne-test/tsconfig/base.json`
through the npm workspace link. Run `npm ci` after switching from the old layout.
The root build still emits CommonJS JavaScript and declarations under `dist/`;
source behavior and effective compiler settings are unchanged.

`package:deployment` performs a clean build, then writes
`releases/commerce.tar.gz` containing compiled `dist/` modules, their package
metadata, and this documentation. `dist/package.json` explicitly declares
CommonJS so the modules also load when extracted inside an ESM consumer project.
`deploy/README.md` is a relative symlink to this file; the archive
preserves it. Sources, node_modules, Git metadata, and old build files are excluded.
The executable `deploy/package.sh` also works from another working directory.
A failed build or archive operation exits nonzero and leaves the previous
successful archive intact. Only use the archive after a successful command.

Extract the bundle into an empty directory and smoke-test it:

```sh
mkdir release
tar -xzf releases/commerce.tar.gz -C release
node -e "console.log(require('./release/dist/apps/api/src').health())"
```

The API and worker are reusable modules, not running services. Consumers load
`dist/apps/api/src/index.js` or `dist/apps/worker/src/index.js`; they require no
runtime npm dependencies. This process does not deploy a server or provision
infrastructure. Run one packaging process per checkout because the build output
is shared.

The build workflow runs on pull requests, pushes to main, and manual dispatch.
It installs dependencies, runs config and packaging checks, and uploads the tar
archive as a GitHub Actions artifact with seven-day retention. It has read-only
repository contents permissions and performs no environment deployment.

"build": "npm run clean && tsc -p tsconfig.build.json",
    "test:config": "sh tooling/tests/workspace-config.test.sh",
    "test:deployment": "sh deploy/tests/package.test.sh",
    "test": "npm run test:config && npm run test:deployment",
    "package:deployment": "./deploy/package.sh"

# Commerce operations PR review repository

This deterministic TypeScript workspace models checkout, inventory reservations,
payments, cancellation, outbox delivery, job leases, and reservation expiry. It
uses in-memory state and injected clocks and IDs so pull-request analysis is
stable.

```sh
npm ci
npm run build
```

The repository is intentionally outside Daphne's tracked source. Its local Git
history supplies exact BASE and HEAD commits and can later be published for a
real pull-request run. Scenario tooling and answer keys live in the sibling
`commerce-fixture/` directory so Daphne cannot see them in analyzed source.

The model exercises explicit interleavings only. It does not claim database
transaction isolation or distributed delivery guarantees.
